evidence.quote: Be it enacted by the Legislature of the state of Utah:

summary.short: S.B. 226 (2025) adds Utah Code 13-75 on generative artificial intelligence in consumer transactions and regulated services. Suppliers must disclose AI use when asked, and regulated-occupation providers must disclose high-risk AI interactions. Violations are enforced by the Division of Consumer Protection with fines and court remedies, effective 05/07/25.
summary.long: S.B. 226 (2025) creates Utah Code 13-75 on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in consumer transactions and regulated services, effective 05/07/25. It defines generative AI and high-risk AI interactions. A supplier using generative AI must disclose that the individual is interacting with AI and not a human when the individual asks. Individuals in regulated occupations must prominently disclose generative AI use in high-risk interactions, verbally or in writing, and must comply with occupational requirements. A violation of the chapter is a violation of the consumer protection provision in Subsection 13-11-4(1), and it is no defense that generative AI made, undertook or furthered the violative act. A safe harbor protects a person from enforcement under the disclosure section if the generative AI clearly and conspicuously discloses its nature, and the Division of Consumer Protection may make rules on disclosure forms. The Division director may impose an administrative fine of up to $2,500 per violation. The Division may sue for injunctions, disgorgement and fines of up to $2,500 per violation. A person who violates an administrative or court order faces a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation. The bill also extends the repeal date of the Artificial Intelligence Policy Act to July 1, 2027 and repeals Section 13-2-12.

relations.note: Amends the section to change the repeal date in subsection (5) of Title 13, Chapter 72 (Artificial Intelligence Policy Act) from May 1, 2025 to July 1, 2027. The bill header gives the prior text as last amended by Laws of Utah 2024, Third Special Session, Chapter 5.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes legal treatment was found. The dollar amounts in Sec. 13-75-105 (up to $2,500 administrative fine, up to $2,500 court fine, up to $5,000 civil penalty) are penalty maxima and are coded under enforcement. Dates in Sec. 7 and Sec. 9 are events, not thresholds.
